verdict.summary: A Private app needs no approval and can be shared with any Pipedrive company through a direct install link, so a working multi-customer OAuth app is a same-day job once you have a developer sandbox. A Marketplace listing (Public app) is optional but takes up to 21 business days of review, and the app type can't be changed after creation.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Assumes the sandbox request form is processed quickly; the docs don't state a turnaround.

timeToProd.assumes: A Private app shared via its unlisted install link, which is enough for an agent reading and writing CRM data; a Marketplace (Public) listing adds up to 21 business days of review.
timeToProd.waitingOn: Nothing — no review for Private apps

prerequisites.why: The Developer Hub, where you register the app and get client_id/client_secret, is reached through a sandbox. It's limited to 5 seats and deleted if inactive (no app within 45 days, or no live app within 6 months).
Apps must use OAuth 2.0 with server-side code; redirect_uri must match the callback URL registered for the app.

prerequisites.item: For a Public (Marketplace) app: Terms of Service, Privacy Policy, pricing page, demo video and test accounts
prerequisites.why: Required by the pre-submission checklist, along with membership in the Pipedrive Developers' Community and acceptance of the Developer Partner Agreement.

scopeTiers.impact: Enough for an agent that answers questions about deals, people and activities. No scope-specific approval is documented.
Create and update records. Users must accept or deny all scopes together, so ask only for what you need.

scopeTiers.time: Same day (Private) / up to 21 business days (Public)
scopeTiers.impact: No special approval documented, but Marketplace reviewers check that you request only needed scopes, and mail access is likely to draw scrutiny.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: The scrutiny claim is our inference.

scopeTiers.impact: Manage pipelines, fields, users and webhooks. The installing user needs admin rights, but the Marketplace doesn't block non-admin installs, so your app has to handle that case (check GET /users/{id}/permissions).

steps.title: Request a developer sandbox
steps.detail: Fill in the sandbox form on the developers site and sign in to the sandbox company.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Turnaround isn't stated in the docs.

steps.title: Choose Private vs Public carefully
steps.detail: Private: shared via direct install link, no review, no listing. Public: Marketplace listing after approval. The app type can't be changed later in Developer Hub.

steps.title: Register the app in Developer Hub
steps.detail: In the sandbox, open Developer Hub, create the app, set the callback URL and scopes, and copy client_id and client_secret.

steps.title: Implement the OAuth flow
steps.detail: Redirect to https://oauth.pipedrive.com/oauth/authorize?client_id=...&redirect_uri=...&state=...; exchange the code (valid 5 min) at POST https://oauth.pipedrive.com/oauth/token with HTTP Basic auth and form encoding. Send API calls to the api_domain returned in the token response.

steps.title: Implement refresh and uninstall handling
steps.detail: Refresh when the 60-minute access token expires; the refresh token lasts 60 days from last use. Handle user_denied and uninstall, and clean up stored tokens.

steps.title: Design for the token-based rate budget
steps.detail: Prefer webhooks and API v2 (cheaper per call) over polling, cache lookups, and back off on 429s. Search is capped at 10 requests per 2 seconds.

steps.title: Make the Private app live and share the install link
steps.detail: Set the Private app live in Developer Hub and give customers the direct installation link. Each user in a company installs it themselves.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The exact console button label wasn't observed.

steps.title: Optional: prepare Marketplace listing materials
steps.detail: Draft the description, install instructions, pricing page, ToS, privacy policy, and scope rationale; plan the demo video covering permissions and key features.

steps.title: Optional: record demo, provide test accounts, send to review
steps.detail: Record the demo video, create working test accounts, preview the listing and click 'Send to review'.

steps.title: Optional: Marketplace review
steps.detail: Public app reviews may take up to 21 business days. After approval the app is unlisted by default; click Publish in Developer Hub to list it.

agentCanDo: Implement the authorize/token/refresh flow and api_domain routing
Build install, uninstall and permission-check flows
Design webhook-based sync within the token budget
Draft Marketplace listing copy, ToS, privacy policy and scope rationale
Probe the OAuth endpoints and handle error responses
humanMustDo: Request the developer sandbox and sign in
Create the app in Developer Hub and pick Private or Public
Copy client credentials and make the app live
Record the demo video and submit for review (Public only)
Customer side: each user installs the app for their company

blockers.symptom: Need to switch an app from Private to Public (or back)
blockers.cause: The app type can't be changed after creation in Developer Hub.
blockers.fix: Create a new app of the right type and migrate users to its install link.

blockers.symptom: HTTP 429 for every call until midnight
blockers.cause: The company's shared daily token budget (30,000 × plan multiplier × seats) is used up, shared with all other integrations.
blockers.fix: Cut polling, use webhooks and cheaper v2 endpoints, or have the customer buy API token top-ups.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The reset happens at midnight in the server's timezone.

blockers.symptom: Connection dies and refresh returns an error after a long idle period
blockers.cause: The refresh token expires if unused for 60 days.
blockers.fix: Refresh periodically even when idle, or prompt the user to reinstall the app.

blockers.symptom: Admin-only calls fail for some installs
blockers.cause: The admin scope needs an admin installer, but non-admins can still install.
blockers.fix: Check GET /users/{id}/permissions after install and degrade gracefully.

blockers.cause: Sandboxes are deleted if no app is created within 45 days, or no app goes live within 6 months.
blockers.fix: Create an app early and make the Private app live, or sign in and keep it active.

blockers.symptom: {"error":"invalid_request","message":"Invalid request: content must be application/x-www-form-urlencoded"} from the token endpoint
blockers.cause: The token request was sent as JSON or without a body.
blockers.fix: POST form-encoded with HTTP Basic client credentials.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: Observed with an empty POST on 2026-10-20.

nuances.text: Access tokens last 60 minutes (use expires_in). Refresh tokens expire after 60 days unused; each refresh resets that window and returns the same refresh token. Auth codes last 5 minutes.
Installs are per user and per company: each user installs the app themselves, and a user in several companies installs it for each one.

OAuth apps get four times the burst limit of API-token integrations (e.g. 80 vs 20 requests per 2 s on Lite), but share the same company daily token budget. Search costs 40 tokens and is limited to 10 requests per 2 s.
The approval checklist forbids storing or unnecessarily using user API tokens, so an agent should rely on OAuth, not ask users for personal API tokens.

Pipedrive's docs describe Private apps both as shareable with 'any Pipedrive company' and as the route for apps 'used only internally'. Whether broad commercial distribution via Private apps is acceptable under the Developer Partner Agreement isn't spelled out.
There's no OIDC discovery document at oauth.pipedrive.com; this is plain OAuth 2.0, not OpenID Connect.
